subject: general
question: What was the main aim of the agreement made by UNEP in 1987?

options.text: To use more CFCs in fire extinguishers
To stop emission of greenhouse gases
To freeze the production of CFCs at 1986 level

solution:
The correct answer is __**to freeze the production of CFCs at 1986 level**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The main aim of the agreement made by UNEP in 1987 was **to freeze the production of CFCs at the 1986 level**.
 
• This agreement is known as the **Montreal Protocol** on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer.
 
• The protocol was designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of numerous substances responsible for ozone depletion, primarily chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).
 
• The Montreal Protocol is considered one of the most successful environmental agreements to date.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)** facilitated the Montreal Protocol, which was agreed upon on **September 16, 1987**, and entered into force on **January 1, 1989**.
 
• As of today, the protocol has undergone several amendments and adjustments to include more substances and to accelerate the phase-out schedules.
 
• The Montreal Protocol has significantly contributed to the recovery of the ozone layer and is a model for international cooperation on environmental issues.
 
• Due to its success, September 16 is celebrated as **International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer**.
